subject: SCIENCE
title: Plants Help Life
objective: Explain ways plants support living systems.
introduction: Mangoes, shade, and fresh air — plants give us so much! How do plants help living things?

vocabulary.definition: A living thing that grows in soil and makes food.
The natural home of a plant or animal.
What something is made of, like wood or plastic.

items.prompt: Which statement about how plants help is true?

options.text: Every plant is safe to eat
Plants make sugars through photosynthesis and can provide food, oxygen, shade, habitat, and materials.

items.explanation: Plants use light to make their own food and give us food, oxygen, shade, and homes for animals. Not every plant is safe to eat, and plants do not eat soil.

items.prompt: Which example shows a way plants help?

options.text: trees grow in a single day

items.explanation: A tree's leaves and branches block the Sun, giving shade. Trees do not eat animals, and they take years to grow.

items.prompt: Which statement is not true?  (in this lesson: Plants Help Life)
items.explanation: Plants make their own food with light — they do not eat soil. Trees do give shade, and plants do form homes for animals.

items.prompt: What do plants generally make through photosynthesis?
items.explanation: Using light, water, and air, plants make sugars — their own food. They do not make plastic or soil.

items.prompt: Which way do plants help living things?
items.explanation: Fruits, vegetables, and grains come from plants, so plants help feed us. Plants need water, and they make their own food.
